compiled_state.title: test_interactivity_gates_complex_escalation passes locally but fails in CI (environmental flake)
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Description

`tests/scripts/test-debug-everything-interactivity.sh::test_interactivity_gates_complex_escalation` passes consistently when run locally (8/0) but fails consistently in CI on PRs #227 and #228 (1 fail). Same source file, same git commit, same test content — different environment, different result.

## Symptoms

- Local: `bash tests/scripts/test-debug-everything-interactivity.sh` → PASSED: 8 FAILED: 0
- CI (ubuntu-latest, Python 3.13.13, ubuntu bash): FAIL — "non-interactive mode logs COMPLEX_ESCALATION as ticket comment: expected found, actual missing"
- Re-run does not change CI result (consistent failure, not transient)
- Test PASSES on main with main's debug-everything/SKILL.md
- Test FAILS in CI on session branch and story branches that include the SKILL.md edits from commit 4c730cf6db (bad-fix) or 6ac0b1fc48 (KNOWN GAP edits)

## Investigation done (session 2026-05-18)

- Replicated the test's Python regex extraction locally on multiple branches — extracted section is identical in local runs and (presumably) CI runs
- The bash regex with shopt nocasematch matches the pattern in local runs
- Could not identify environmental difference between local (macOS, bash 5.x) and CI (ubuntu-latest)
- Suspected causes (unverified): bash version difference, locale/encoding difference, test runner sequencing/parallelism exposing ordering dependency, or python regex behavior difference

## Decision (user 2026-05-18)

The assertion is skipped via Option A: the test function early-returns with a SKIP echo so CI passes. This unblocks epic b575 merge cascade. The underlying brittleness is tracked here for dedicated investigation.

## Suggested remediation

1. Determine WHY the test behaves differently in CI vs locally — reproduce locally if possible (run in ubuntu container, in CI-like environment)
2. If the regex-based text-parsing test is the wrong abstraction, replace with a behavioral test that exercises the actual non-interactive deferral path (mock INTERACTIVE_SESSION=false, run complex-escalation-handler.md, assert the gh ticket comment subprocess call was made)
3. Re-enable the assertion in test-debug-everything-interactivity.sh

## Related

- Discovered during epic b575 merge cascade work
